caption: William Tyndale's cell at Vilvoorde in the winter of 1535–36. He asked for a candle, warmer clothes and his Hebrew Bible.
alt: A man seen from behind sits at a rough table in a stone cell, writing by one candle beneath a small barred window.

caption: A Passover table near the end of the Seder: a cup set apart for Elijah and the door opened to the night.
alt: A table with candles, unleavened bread and a full cup stands before an open door through which night sky and stars are visible.

caption: Asael Smith writing his letter to his family, April 10, 1799. The candlelit room is imagined; the letter survives.
alt: A man in an eighteenth-century coat writes by candlelight at a small table in a plain farmhouse room.

caption: Solomon Mack, in his seventy-sixth year, confined to his bed by rheumatism in the winter of 1810–11. He wrote that he saw a light and felt his heart change.
alt: An old man lies in a bed beneath a window in a dim farmhouse room, with soft light falling near his pillow.

caption: Lydia Gates Mack, a former schoolteacher, gathered her children morning and evening to teach them to pray.
alt: A mother sits by a hearth while several children kneel around her in prayer.

caption: Tunbridge, Vermont, in the 1790s, where the Smiths cleared a farm on stony hill country.
alt: A small house and rail fence on a rolling hillside, with stone walls, stumps and forested ridges behind.

caption: Lucy Mack Smith, gravely ill in Randolph, Vermont, about 1802–3, pleaded with the Lord through the night and covenanted to serve Him.
alt: A young woman lies in bed, propped against pillows in a dark room, with a faint glow near the window.

caption: Lucy's dream: two trees beside a clear stream, one bending gracefully in the wind and one standing stiff. She took them to mean her husband and his brother Jesse.
alt: Two tall trees on a meadow beside a winding stream; one bends gracefully in the wind while the other stands rigid.

caption: The Smiths' rented farmhouse near Sharon, Vermont, where Joseph Smith Jr. was born on December 23, 1805.
alt: A small farmhouse in a snowy valley at dusk, with smoke rising from the chimney and wooded hills behind.

caption: Lebanon, New Hampshire, about 1813. During the operation Lucy walked several hundred yards from the house so that she would not hear.
alt: A woman in a shawl stands alone in a field with her back to a distant farmhouse, her hands clasped.

sec: "As Sure As There Is a God in Heaven"
caption: Winter of 1816–17: Lucy and her eight children traveled some three hundred miles over snowy roads toward Palmyra, New York.
alt: A covered wagon drawn by a horse moves along a snowy road through bare trees, with a woman and children walking beside it.

sec: A Log House in the Woods
caption: The Smiths' log house on their Manchester land south of Palmyra, about 1818–19, surrounded by forest they cleared acre by acre.
alt: A log house in a clearing with stumps and felled trees, surrounded by tall forest.

caption: Spring 1820: fourteen-year-old Joseph reading James 1:5 in the family's log house.
alt: A boy seen from behind reads a large Bible by the light of a fire in a log-walled room.

caption: A grove of tall hardwoods west of the Smith log house, the place Joseph went to pray. Joseph called it a beautiful, clear day early in the spring.
alt: A grove of tall, straight hardwood trunks with morning light slanting between them.

caption: The First Vision, as Joseph described it: a pillar of light, brighter than the sun, descending until it rested on him. Out of reverence the sketch shows the light, not the Personages.
alt: A boy kneels among tall trees, seen from behind, as a column of brilliant light descends toward him from above.

caption: September 21, 1823: Joseph said that light filled his room and a messenger, Moroni, stood beside his bed. The messenger is shown here only as light.
alt: A young man kneels beside a bed under a sloping attic ceiling while a standing form of light fills the room.

caption: The hill about three miles from the Smith farm, where Joseph found a large rounded stone near the top on the west side.
alt: A wooded hillside with a large rounded stone near its crest; a lone young man climbs toward it.

caption: Autumn 1823: the Smith family gathered in the evenings to listen as Joseph told what he had learned. Lucy remembered how closely they listened.
alt: A family sits in a circle around a hearth in a log room, all turned toward a young man who is speaking.

caption: Harmony, Pennsylvania, 1828: Emma Smith served as scribe while Joseph dictated the translation.
alt: A young woman writes at a small table by a window in a plain room, a quill in her hand and pages before her.

sec: On the Banks of the Susquehanna
caption: May 15, 1829: Joseph and Oliver Cowdery prayed in the woods near the river. They testified that John the Baptist appeared and conferred the Aaronic Priesthood. He is shown here as light.
alt: Two young men kneel in a wooded clearing by a river, bathed in light from a bright form standing before them.

caption: Egbert B. Grandin's printing office in Palmyra, 1829–30, where five thousand copies of the Book of Mormon were printed and bound.
alt: A wooden hand press stands in a print shop beside stacks of printed sheets and bound books.

caption: Tuesday, April 6, 1830: neighbors and friends gathered at Peter and Mary Whitmer's log home in Fayette, New York, to organize the church.
alt: People in early nineteenth-century dress walk toward a log farmhouse in early spring, some arriving by wagon.

caption: Spring 1830: Samuel Smith set out on foot with a knapsack of Books of Mormon. A copy he left with Rhoda Greene later reached her brother Brigham Young.
alt: A young man with a knapsack walks along a country road between fields and a rail fence.

caption: February 4, 1831: a sleigh pulled up to Newel K. Whitney's store in Kirtland, Ohio, and Joseph stepped inside and reached across the counter.
alt: A horse-drawn sleigh stands in the snow before a two-story frame store; a man walks toward its door.

sec: "Shall We … Build a House for Our God of Logs?"
caption: Building the Kirtland Temple, 1833–36. Irregular sandstone blocks were laid in mortar and later covered with stucco, and children gathered broken crockery and glass for the finish coat.
alt: Workers on wooden scaffolding raise rough stone walls of a large gabled building while two children carry a basket of broken crockery.

caption: The Kirtland Temple at its dedication, March 27, 1836. Its stuccoed walls were tinted a bluish gray, with painted lines imitating cut stone.
alt: A two-story gabled temple with tall pointed windows and a square tower, its walls smoothly plastered and lined to suggest stone blocks, with people walking toward it.

caption: April 3, 1836, the day after the second Seder: Joseph and Oliver Cowdery testified that the Savior, then Moses, Elias and Elijah appeared in the temple. Out of reverence the sketch shows only light above the pulpits.
alt: Two men kneel, seen from behind, before tiered wooden pulpits behind a lowered curtain, as brilliant light fills the space above.

caption: January 12, 1838: Joseph and Sidney Rigdon rode south out of Kirtland after dark, covering nearly sixty miles by morning.
alt: Two riders on horseback travel along a road under a winter night sky, with bare trees and a distant hill.

caption: February 1839: with Frederick and Alexander in her arms and Joseph III and Julia holding her skirt, Emma Smith walked across the frozen Mississippi to Illinois.
alt: A woman carrying two small children walks across a frozen river, with two older children holding her skirts and a far shore of bare trees.

caption: The jail at Liberty, Missouri, winter 1838–39. The prisoners lived in the lower room, which had two small barred windows.
alt: A small, square two-story stone jail stands in snow under a gray sky, with tiny barred windows near the ground.

caption: Nauvoo, Illinois, rising on a bend of the Mississippi in the early 1840s.
alt: A river town of houses and gardens spreads across a flat riverbank and up a bluff, with steamboat smoke on the wide river.

caption: The Nauvoo Temple under construction on the bluff, early 1840s. Men gave one day in ten to the work.
alt: A large limestone temple with pilasters rises within wooden scaffolding, as workers haul stone in a wagon.

sec: Before Sunrise on the Mount of Olives
caption: October 24, 1841: Orson Hyde climbed the Mount of Olives before dawn and wrote out a prayer for the land and its people.
alt: A lone man kneels on a rocky hillside among olive trees at dawn, looking toward the walls and domes of Jerusalem across a valley.

caption: March 17, 1842: twenty women met with Joseph Smith in the large room above his red brick store and organized the Female Relief Society of Nauvoo.
alt: Women in bonnets and shawls sit on benches in a plain upper room with windows, while one stands to speak.

caption: Carthage Jail, June 27, 1844. Joseph and Hyrum Smith, John Taylor and Willard Richards spent the hot afternoon in the upstairs room.
alt: A two-story stone jail building on a summer afternoon, its upper windows open, with a single tree beside it.

caption: February 1846: the first Latter-day Saint families crossed the Mississippi from Nauvoo, the temple on the bluff behind them.
alt: Covered wagons on a flatboat ferry cross a wide river toward the viewer, with a pale stone temple and tower on a bluff in the distance.

caption: An open door, an empty chair, a waiting cup: the invitation of Elijah's promise, still extended.
alt: A doorway stands open to a dawn landscape, with light streaming across a table set with a single cup.
